input.command:
python3 -c '
# Pose at obs 83:
# theta = -60 - 30 = -90 deg (= 270 deg, exactly facing -x, west!).
# move = 0.5 along heading -x:
# X = 1.2312 - 0.5 = 0.7312
# Y = 4.5972
# Both chairs along the west wall are clearly in view side-by-side!
# Chair 1 is on the left, Chair 2 is in the middle, Table 1 is on the right, Plant 1 is behind Table 1!
# This gives a perfect direct orthogonal view of both chairs and the west wall!

import cv2, numpy as np
img = cv2.imread("/work/observations/obs_0083.png")

# Find chair 2 (middle chair):
# chair 2 base of legs:
# Let us inspect the columns around x in [180, 250], rows [300, 420]
mask = (img[:,:,2] > 90) & (img[:,:,2] < 160) & (img[:,:,1] > 40) & (img[:,:,1] < 80) & (img[:,:,0] < 40)

# Chair 2: x in [180, 250]
ys2, xs2 = np.where(mask[:, 180:250])
xs2 += 180
print(f"Chair 2 in obs 83: x=[{xs2.min()}, {xs2.max()}], y=[{ys2.min()}, {ys2.max()}], bottom_y={ys2.max()}")

# Chair 1: x in [0, 80]
ys1, xs1 = np.where(mask[:, 0:80])
print(f"Chair 1 in obs 83: x=[{xs1.min()}, {xs1.max()}], y=[{ys1.min()}, {ys1.max()}], bottom_y={ys1.max()}")
'
